A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Geometry-Informed Neural Networks work. All pages, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original neural-shape experiments, Gray-Scott pattern generation and diversity-optimization results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds quantitative model comparisons and ablations in Appendix B, particularly Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The conditional neural fields, constraint-penalty objective, boundary-based diversity distance, minimal aggregation and connectedness Algorithm 1 are retained. The expanded architecture comparisons use existing GINN components rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: The same geometry, reaction-diffusion and annulus demonstrations remain. The mirror task specification changes from focusing rays at (0,1.5) in v1 to focusing at (0,1) with an additional f(0)=0 interface constraint in v2 Section 4.1.

E2.justification: v2 adds SIREN with first-layer frequencies 1 and 2 alongside softplus-MLP in the obstacle comparison, and bracket variants without normal, diversity or eikonal losses. The separate 2D connectedness comparison from v1 Figure 4(c) disappears. These expand internal comparisons; cited persistent-homology methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces quantitative constraint, diversity and smoothness evaluation, including latent-midpoint comparisons. Table 2 revises reported softplus obstacle training from 2000 to 3000 iterations and its eikonal weight from 1e-2 to 1e-5, and adds 64-wide SIREN configurations. The prescribed obstacle normals are also corrected from (0,±1) to (±1,0).

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands architecture, frequency, diversity and interpolation analyses for the obstacle, and adds normal-, diversity- and eikonal-loss ablations for the bracket. Previously qualitative connectedness and initialization tests gain quantitative assessment. The standalone 2D connectedness illustration is removed, while the annulus diversity analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2 averages metrics across 16 obstacle or four bracket shapes from a generator; this is evaluation aggregation, not repeated-training uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 add numerical constraint-satisfaction, diversity and smoothness results absent from v1. Table 3 reports softplus diversity of 0.12 with the diversity loss versus 0.0076 without it. Table 4 reports generative-bracket diversity of 0.061 by default, 0.034 without diversity loss and 0.033 without eikonal loss. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds formal definitions for constraint-evaluation measures, mean shape-set diversity and clipped smoothness. The Morse-theory assumptions, connectedness construction, Algorithm 1 and existing diversity derivation otherwise remain after relocation and renumbering.

C1.justification: The central data-free GINN and generative-PINN claims remain. v2 expands the introduction's contribution description to include evaluation metrics and architecture investigations, while narrowing the connectedness contribution's novelty positioning to a continuous-function alternative to existing topology losses.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking SIREN's spectral bias to diversity and eikonal regularization to more meaningful neural-field distances. It also reinterprets the retained Figure 10 examples: v1 describes failure to structure the bracket latent space, whereas v2 identifies improved interpolation with smoothing and acknowledges that the mechanism remains unresolved.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds GPU-memory estimates of approximately 11 GB for the bracket and 7 GB for the obstacle, identifies Dalmia's SIREN implementation, and documents the added SIREN configurations. Existing GPU types, training-time reports and reaction-diffusion implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v1 Section 3.1.1 says connectedness had not been addressed for implicit neural shapes. v2 acknowledges relevant prior approaches, including Mezghanni et al. (2021), and positions its continuous Morse construction against discretized persistent homology. This substantially revises novelty positioning. It also adds PINN-optimization references and condenses the specific topology-optimization discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, the connectedness explanation is condensed and partly moved into the appendix, and the obstacle narrative is reorganized around generative-model comparisons. The appendices separate implementation from a new evaluation section, and citations change from author-year to numbered references.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a bracket-focused illustration into a four-task overview incorporating earlier material. v2 adds architecture/diversity displays, expanded interpolation comparisons, a normal-loss close-up and quantitative Tables 3–4, while expanding Table 2. Figure 10 retains its examples but moves and receives a substantively revised caption.

improvement.justification: v1 relies mainly on qualitative examples; v2's defined metrics, Tables 3–4 and expanded ablations make constraint violations and diversity tradeoffs assessable, substantially strengthening the empirical foundation. The revised connectedness positioning also improves precision. These gains outweigh localized reporting defects, notably Table 3's purported interface fraction exceeding one and prose describing its approximately 16-fold softplus diversity difference as several orders of magnitude.
